approach: Split the work into a pure measurement, a pure trigger and one model call. (1) status.rs gets `Throughput::compute(&Records)`, which reads only job records. Per landed job it takes stage minutes from Reader (reading), Planner+Critic (planning), Producer and Verifier invocations (ended_at minus started_at), from verification.checks[].duration (checks), and from the tail between the last invocation's end and the landing outcome time (landing and rebuild, one stage, because no record separates a rebuild). It reports landed jobs per UTC day, median total and per-stage minutes over the newest THROUGHPUT_WINDOW=20 landed jobs, idle time (gaps between merged job intervals), and minutes spent on closed non-landed and plan-stopped jobs. It is `StatusView.throughput` with a `text()` method. (2) records.rs gets one new kind, `athena.throughput-review/1`, at `records/throughput-reviews/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json`, modelled on CodeHealthBaseline: landings, window median, trigger, optional proposal (bottleneck, change, expected_minutes_saved, priority, request_job) and followups (predicted vs measured). (3) hestia.rs gets pure `throughput_due`, `priority_for_minutes`, `throughput_followups`, a request builder through `StewardRequest::new`, and `Athena::throughput_review(ui)`, called from `review_passes`. The review writes the section and a copy of docs/design into a scratch workspace, asks the model via agent_spec/invoke_and_record (Role::Steward, models.verifier, as steward/auditor/audience do), validates the JSON, queues one design request unless an open one carries the marker, and commits the review record and invocation together. A model failure still commits a no-proposal review record so cadence advances. (4) code_health.rs: doc comment on `REVIEW_EVERY` names it as the shared cadence; no behavior change. (5) hestia.md holds the cadence, prediction, follow-up and the new record's path/schema (so docs/records.md is not touched); CHANGELOG.md gets the entry. Two files outside the brief's list stay, each with a stated reason: store.rs (Records is a struct with one typed Vec per kind, and the new record cannot be read without a Vec and a load arm; no way around it short of not adding a record kind, which would lose the durable cadence point and prediction) and display.rs (athena status text is built only there, with each section hand-printed; no generic field carries text; without a 3-line print the section would exist in the JSON view only). docs/records.md is dropped from the plan.

decisions.choice: Compute throughput purely from Records (job records), with no git history; the trigger and the status median share THROUGHPUT_WINDOW.
decisions.reason: Records hold invocation started_at/ended_at, verification check durations and outcome.at, so status and the review share one number; tests build Records in memory or commit them with the existing `put` helper.

rejected.option: Count landings from git first-parent history like code_health::landings
rejected.why: Needs a git fixture per test and can disagree with the records-based median it is compared against.
No per-stage split; omits reading, planning and landing.

decisions.choice: Fold landing and rebuild into one stage: outcome.at (later_outcome first) minus the end of the job's last invocation, floored at 0.
decisions.reason: No record separates the post-landing rebuild (drain.rs Steps::rebuild). The doc and text() label say what is measured.

rejected.why: Widens the change into drain.rs and the job record schema; out of scope.

decisions.choice: New record kind athena.throughput-review/1 holding cadence state, prediction and follow-ups; touch store.rs only to add `Records.throughput_reviews`, its load arm and sort.
decisions.reason: Cadence needs a durable last-review point; the prediction must outlive the request. Records is a typed struct, so store.rs must change for the record to be read. The brief's records.rs deliverable already presumes a new kind.

rejected.why: No median, prediction or follow-up fields, and the design review must not change.

rejected.option: Keep the prediction only in request text
rejected.why: The follow-up would parse prose and a closed request would lose it.

rejected.option: Read throughput-review files directly in hestia.rs, bypassing Records and store.rs
rejected.why: Duplicates the loader, skips path/schema validation and makes tests diverge from how every other record is read.

decisions.choice: Print the section in display.rs with `if let Some(t) = &v.throughput { writeln!(out, "{}", t.text()) }` beside check_durations (about 3 lines), and do not touch docs/records.md.
decisions.reason: athena status text is hand-built in display.rs; the request is for a section in athena status. docs/records.md is not read by any test (grep of *.rs found only message strings in status.rs), so the layout line moves into hestia.md, a listed deliverable.

rejected.option: Leave display.rs unchanged and expose the section only in the JSON StatusView
rejected.why: Users running athena status would not see it.

rejected.option: Edit docs/records.md for the layout line
rejected.why: Outside the deliverables and not required by any test; hestia.md can carry the path and schema.

decisions.choice: A cited change is a landed request job, other than the design request itself, whose text contains the review's record id; the request body tells authors to cite that id. Measured minutes = window median of landed jobs landing after the cited job, capped at the newest 10, needing at least 1. A follow-up is written once per review.
decisions.reason: Deterministic and testable from records. The design request lands a note, not the speedup.

rejected.option: Treat the design request's own landing as the cited change

decisions.choice: Priority from expected minutes saved: >=10 urgent, >=5 high, >=2 normal, else low, as named consts in a pure `priority_for_minutes`.

rejected.option: Always urgent like the root-cause request
rejected.why: Brief says priority is set by expected minutes saved.

decisions.choice: Duplicate suppression: a non-Closed request job with a line starting 'Throughput design: ' means no new request; the review still writes its record with request_job empty and a note.
decisions.reason: Matches structural_pass_open; independent of the record having committed, so a crash cannot cause a duplicate.

rejected.option: Skip the whole review while a request is open
rejected.why: Cadence would stall and a follow-up could not be recorded.

decisions.choice: Call throughput_review from review_passes with a third summary line; it never fails the caller.
decisions.reason: review_passes is the existing housekeeping at drain start and in sweeps; the pure trigger means normal drains make no model call.

rejected.why: Puts a strong-model wait inside the landing path the review exists to shorten.

decisions.choice: Use Role::Steward and models.verifier with no new Role and no config change.
decisions.reason: A new Role ripples through Role::as_str, budgets and match arms; athena.toml is out of scope.

risks.risk: A model call in review_passes fires in existing drain or sweep tests that script the fake driver.
risks.mitigation: The call runs only when throughput_due is true, which needs at least 10 landed request jobs. Run the full cargo test; if a fixture reaches 10 landings, give it a prior review record.

risks.risk: Model failure or malformed answer retries and spends money on every drain.
risks.mitigation: A no-proposal review record with a note is committed on any failure, which advances the cadence; the invocation record is always committed.

risks.risk: Median over a small window is noisy and triggers 'worsened' spuriously.
risks.mitigation: The window is 20 landed jobs, the trigger needs at least one new landing, and each review stores the current median as the next baseline.

risks.risk: A crash between queuing the request and committing the review record leaves an open request with no record.
risks.mitigation: Suppression looks at the open request's marker line, not the record, so no second request is queued. That review gets no follow-up, which is noted as acceptable.

risks.risk: Model text with bullet-like lines is refused by StewardRequest::new.
risks.mitigation: Flatten model text with `one_line` before it enters the body; if the builder still errors, record the proposal without a request and a note.

risks.risk: Adding a StatusView field or AnyRecord variant breaks exhaustive matches or struct literals elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Grep showed AnyRecord::CodeHealthBaseline handled only in records.rs, store.rs and code_health.rs; cargo clippy --all-targets finds any other site.

risks.risk: Touching store.rs and display.rs widens scope beyond the brief's list.
risks.mitigation: Both edits are minimal and mechanical (one Vec, one load arm, one sort; one print block), each tied to a stated need; docs/records.md was removed from the plan.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in status.rs over an in-memory `Records` (JobRecords fields are pub): 3 landed jobs on two UTC days with Reader/Planner/Critic/Producer/Verifier invocations of known started_at/ended_at, verification checks of known durations, outcome.at at known offsets; one Rejected job and one plan-stopped job with known spans; gaps between job intervals and one overlap. Calls `Throughput::compute(&records)` (pure, no seam needed; added by step 3) and asserts the struct fields and the `text()` string that display.rs prints.
demonstrations.observes: Exact numbers: landed per day (e.g. 2 and 1), median total minutes, medians for reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier and landing/rebuild, idle minutes (overlap gives 0), minutes on non-landed jobs.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without Throughput::compute the test does not compile; a mis-attributed stage (planner counted as producer) or wrong idle merging fails the exact per-stage assertions.

demonstrations.method: Test in hestia.rs using the existing temp-repo helper `athena_in`, changed to take a driver. Entry point `Athena::throughput_review(&TestUi)`; guards: not nested and `throughput_due` true. Seam: `FakeAgentDriver::new(script)` (exists today; used in run/mod.rs and test_support.rs; hestia.rs athena_in uses `FakeAgentDriver::deterministic()`), script returns `FakeTurn::output(json!({bottleneck, stage, change, expected_minutes_saved, rationale}))` and counts calls. Seed 10 landed jobs with `put`. Run the review, then seed 10 more landings and run again. The double only returns canned JSON; request building, validation and suppression are production code.
demonstrations.observes: After the first run exactly one open request job whose text has the marker line, bottleneck, proposed change and predicted minutes; one throughput-review record with the proposal and request job id. After the second run still one request, a second review record with request_job None and a note; model called once per review.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without duplicate suppression the second run queues a second request and the open-request count fails; without the StewardRequest call no request exists.

demonstrations.method: Table test of pure `throughput_due(landed_count, window_median, latest_review)` with constructed review records, plus a test through `Athena::throughput_review` with a counting fake driver (same seam as criterion 2).
demonstrations.observes: No prior review: 9 landed gives None, 10 gives Cadence. Prior review at 10 landings: 19 landed and equal median None, 20 landed Cadence. Prior median 10.0: current 12.0 None (20% is not more than 20%), 12.1 with a new landing Worsened, 12.1 with no new landing None, improved median None. Zero model calls and nothing queued when not due; one call when due.
demonstrations.fails_without: A cadence of 9 or 11, a >= comparison at 20%, or firing on every drain fails a boundary assertion or the call-count assertion.

demonstrations.method: Test in hestia.rs. Commit with `put` a first review record R (median 20.0, proposal predicted saving 6.0, request_job J), a landed request job C whose text contains R and lands later than R, and 3 later landed jobs with known shorter spans. Run `Athena::throughput_review` with the fake driver past the 10-landing mark; also call pure `throughput_followups`. Seam as criterion 2.
demonstrations.observes: The new review record's followups holds one entry for R: predicted 6.0, baseline 20.0, measured window median (e.g. 15.0) and measured saving 5.0. A third review adds no second follow-up for R. A cited change not yet landed records none. J itself, once landed, is not treated as the cited change.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the follow-up step, followups is empty and the predicted-against-measured assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Test pure `priority_for_minutes` at 0.5, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0 and 25.0, and run `Athena::throughput_review` in two temp repos with the fake model predicting 12.0 and 1.0 (seam as criterion 2), reading the queued request text and `Records::priority()`.
demonstrations.observes: Mapping low, normal, high, urgent, urgent; the 12.0 request carries `Priority: urgent` and the 1.0 request `Priority: low`; priority is non-decreasing over an increasing series.
demonstrations.fails_without: A constant priority gives both requests the same level and the assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks as separate simple commands: the one listed here is the test run; fmt and clippy are run the same way (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`). The tests that carry the behavior are those of criteria 1 to 5 and 8, so the full run also proves that the new StatusView field, AnyRecord variant, Records field and review_passes call break no existing status, display, records, drain, sweep, code_health or steward test.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. Existing drain and sweep tests still pass because throughput_due needs 10 landed jobs and fixtures that reach 10 get a prior review record.
demonstrations.fails_without: A new AnyRecord variant left unhandled in a match, a missing StatusView field in a struct literal, a clippy warning, unformatted code, or a drain/sweep test hitting the model call through review_passes makes the corresponding command exit non-zero.

demonstrations.method: New records.rs test modelled on `a_hestia_sweep_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips`: build a ThroughputReview with a proposal and a follow-up, wrap in `AnyRecord::ThroughputReview`, assert schema, canonical_path `records/throughput-reviews/<month>/<id>.json`, and a JSON round trip through `check_record_file(path, bytes)`; a misplaced path gives Misplaced; NaN median or empty bottleneck is refused by validate.

open_questions: No record separates the rebuild after a landing from the landing, so 'landing and rebuild' is one measured tail. Splitting it needs a new timing record in drain.rs, out of scope. Is the combined stage acceptable?
The strong model is models.verifier, as for steward, auditor and audience; athena.toml has no separate strong-model setting. Confirm that is meant.
throughput_review runs in review_passes (drain start and sweeps), so the model wait falls at the next drain start, not at the landing. Is that acceptable?
Whether test_support already has an Invocation or Verification fixture builder was not checked; the producer should grep before writing one.
Whether any other integration test (crates/athena-cli/tests) builds a StatusView literal or matches AnyRecord exhaustively was not fully checked; cargo clippy --all-targets will show it.
